selection_rationale.proposal_001: Primary exploit aligned with evidence, smallest in-block invariant refinement and best chance to recover source-level Q without destabilizing training.
selection_rationale.proposal_002: Second exploit keeps the same bounded family but shifts emphasis to residual calibration, giving a complementary low-risk refinement path.
selection_rationale.proposal_004: Jump candidate for a very narrow late invariant many-body summary, directly matching the evidence brief's only endorsed bounded jump.
selection_rationale.proposal_005: Alternative jump exploring the same late-summary idea in a slightly different placement, preserving diversity among bounded jump implementations.
selection_rationale.proposal_006: Hybrid jump/exploit path combining stream refinement with a narrow invariant summary, offering the strongest upside among non-wildcard expansion options.
selection_rationale.proposal_007: Backward-simplify slot to test whether stripping some late complexity restores benchmark balance after generation_006 regressions.
selection_rationale.proposal_008: Required control proposal to anchor attribution against the source continuation and quantify drift from proposal-writing choices.
selection_rationale.proposal_009: Best wildcard because it stays within the local balanced regime while probing a distinct scalar-normalized refinement, adding breadth without violating evidence constraints.

rejection_rationale.proposal_003: Redundant exploit relative to proposals 001 and 002, with less distinct coverage under the eight-slot budget.
rejection_rationale.proposal_010: Wildcard is weaker and less evidence-grounded than proposal_009, so it loses the final diversity slot.
